question: Who lost the 2021 NBA Finals? Show a table.
raw_answer:
The Phoenix Suns lost the 2021 NBA Finals.

| Game | Date | Winner | Loser | Score |
|------|------|--------|-------|-------|
| Game 1 | July 6, 2021 | Phoenix Suns | Milwaukee Bucks | 118-105 |
| Game 2 | July 7, 2021 | Phoenix Suns | Milwaukee Bucks | 110-104 |
| Game 3 | July 10, 2021 | Milwaukee Bucks | Phoenix Suns | 109-103 |
| Game 4 | July 13, 2021 | Milwaukee Bucks | Phoenix Suns | 109-103 |
| Game 5 | July 17, 2021 | Milwaukee Bucks | Phoenix Suns | 123-119 |
| Game 6 | July 20, 2021 | Milwaukee Bucks | Phoenix Suns | 105-98 |

The Milwaukee Bucks won the series 4-2 and were crowned champions [4].

passages.heading: Game 5
passages.text: Milwaukee became the first team in the series to win on the road.<sup>[52]</sup> Antetokounmpo, Holiday, and Middleton combined for 88 points, becoming the fifth trio to each score 25 points on 50% shooting in a single Finals game, and the first to accomplish the feat since the Lakers' Abdul-Jabbar (36 points), James Worthy (33), and Magic Johnson (26) in 1985.<sup>[57]</sup> Phoenix lost three straight games for only the second time in the season, the first occurring six months earlier.<sup>[56]</sup> Paul ended the game with 21 points, 11 assists and one turnover,<sup>[55]</sup> while Ayton finished with 20 points and 10 rebounds. Booker became the first player in the Finals to score at least 40 in consecutive games and lose both.<sup>[54]</sup> Antetokounmpo and he were the first pair of players to score 40+ twice in the same Finals.<sup>[57]</sup> Bucks' role player Thanasis Antetokounmpo, the older brother of Giannis, and assistant coach Josh Oppenheimer were away from the team due to COVID-19 health and safety protocols. The NBA also replaced referee Sean Wright after he entered health and safety protocols.<sup>[52]</sup>
